title: Sequence-length-aware batching playbook — arch review notes
body:
Meeting: Architecture review (design playbook)
Date: 2025-11-06 10:00-11:15 PST
Location: Zoom + #eng-serving-runtime
Note-taker: Aisha Patel

Purpose / context:
- This is an architecture review to agree on a practical playbook for sequence-length-aware batching (SLAB) and eviction behavior that meets our p99 latency SLOs while minimizing cost regressions. We want a recipe teams can apply across hosted/dedicated/private deployments.
- Follow-up to earlier RFC-78 (design intent). Today we focused on tradeoffs, simulation results, and rollout strategy.

Attendees (present):
- Aisha Patel (owner)
- Ethan Morrison (serving-runtime)
- Priya Desai (infer-optimization)
- Marco Ruiz (platform-routing)
- Chen Li (sre)
- Sara Novak (product-hosted-api)
- Quick drop-ins: Ben K. (benchmarks) for 15m

Background / problem summary:
- Uniform batching hurts tail latency when seq length distribution is multimodal (e.g., lots of short requests + occasional long ones). Current continuous-batcher groups by arrival time only; long requests cause blocking and p99 spikes.
- Customers running LLMs with variable prompts see tail latency regressions after traffic growth. We need an operational playbook: detection, policy, safe rollout.

Goals for playbook:
1) Keep p50/p95 mostly unchanged, reduce p99 by 30-60% for mixed distributions.
2) Avoid >10% increase in overall GPU token-cost or throughput loss for common workloads.
3) Provide deterministic rollback and observability hooks.
4) Compatible with both hosted and dedicated pools; no private-only changes.

Alternatives considered (short list):
A) Strict length-bucket batching: dynamically maintain buckets (0-64,65-256,257-1024,>1024) and only batch within bucket; prefer small buckets for latency-critical routes.
   - Pros: simplest to reason about; good tail isolation.
   - Cons: could reduce effective batch sizes -> cost increase for long-batch workloads; needs realtime routing updates.

B) Predictive admission + early-release: allow mixed batches but if a long request is detected (via pre-seed or early token pattern) we release short-request subset early using partial-kv-cache trick.
   - Pros: higher GPU utilization, keeps cost low.
   - Cons: complex kernel changes; risk of correctness if states not synced; longer implementation time.

C) Hybrid soft isolation: use a scoring model per request (expected remaining length) and use a timer threshold (X ms) to flush batches; adjust score thresholds per route.
   - Pros: smooth tradeoffs, easier to tune per-route.
   - Cons: more moving parts; parameter explosion across tenants.

Simulation summary (Ben's simulations run 2025-11-03 -> 2025-11-05):
- Workloads simulated: chat-like multi-turn (70% short <64, 20% mid, 10% long >512), single-turn long-query (heavy tail), embeddings-mix test.
- Baseline: current continuous-batcher.
- Metric focus: p50/p95/p99 latency, tokens-per-second (throughput), GPU utilization, avg batch size.

Key numbers (approx, median of runs):
- Baseline p99: 1.9s
- A) buckets p99: 1.05s (p99 improvement ~45%), throughput -8%, batch size -12% on long workloads.
- B) predictive early-release p99: 0.9s, throughput -2%, implementation high risk.
- C) hybrid soft-isolation p99: 1.1s, throughput -4%, easier to tune.
- Cost impact (estimated token-cost): A) +8%, B) +1.5%, C) +4%

Decision (consensus):
- Move forward with C) Hybrid soft isolation as the default playbook for rollout. Rationale: best balance of latency improvement vs. cost/implementation effort, and provides per-route knobs product can expose. However, we will prototyping B) predictive early-release in parallel as a tech debt/next-phase improvement (low priority but high impact if stable).

Accepted constraints / design commitments:
- Any batching change must expose the following runtime metrics: batch-size-by-length-bucket, batch-flush-reason (timer/size/score), per-route p50/p95/p99, avg-kv-cache-hit-ratio.
- Feature to be behind a per-route feature flag and service-level config. Default for existing routes should be off; enable for a limited set of internal traffic first.
- Must include a 'safe-fallback' that reverts to baseline continuous-batcher on any error or if p99 increases by >10% for 10m window.
- Implementation must not require kernel-level changes for initial rollout (i.e., use existing runtime hooks). If B) ends up required, then kernel work will be scheduled in a separate RFC.

Rollout plan (high level):
Phase 0 - prototype + unit tests (2 weeks)
  - Implement scoring model and per-route timer in a branch. Simple heuristic: expected_remaining_tokens = length_estimator(prompt_tokens); score = expected_remaining_tokens / max_expected.
  - Add metrics scaffolding.
  - Owner: Ethan; target: 2025-11-20

Phase 1 - internal canary (2 weeks)
  - Enable on canary cluster behind flag; feed traffic from internal test harness + 5 internal customers.
  - Monitor p99, throughput, GPU util, cost delta.
  - Owner: Marco + Chen; target: 2025-12-04

Phase 2 - limited public beta (3 weeks)
  - Opt-in for customer routes via console; provide docs and per-route knobs (flush-timer-ms, score-threshold).
  - Product will coordinate comms.
  - Owner: Sara (product) + Priya (runtime); target: 2025-12-25

Phase 3 - default opt-out (4 weeks)
  - Evaluate metrics; if stable, flip default for newly created routes; existing routes remain opt-in for 2 more months.

Monitoring / observability checklist (must ship with feature):
- Dashboards: per-pool and per-route latency distributions, batch-size heatmaps, flush-reason breakdown.
- Alerts: p99 regression >10% for 10m; average batch-size drop >25% for 30m; unhandled errors in batching pipeline.
- Tracing: link request ID -> batch ID -> kernel invocation; log flush events with reason and score.
- Cost dashboard: tokens/kgpu-hour delta by route.

Action items (owners + due dates):
- Ethan: push initial branch with score-based batching + unit tests (due 2025-11-20).
- Priya: produce microbench that validates correctness for partial release vs full release (due 2025-11-24).
- Ben: run longer 24h simulation with customer traffic traces and export results to benchboard (due 2025-11-17).
- Marco: prepare canary infra and a failover path that can switch entire canary cluster back to baseline in <60s (due 2025-11-28).
- Chen: design the alerting playbook for rollback and run a tabletop drill (due 2025-12-02).
- Sara: draft customer documentation and console UX for per-route knobs (initial draft due 2025-11-21).

Open questions / unresolved items:
- How to handle multi-tenant GPU queues where tenancy mixing could still cause long-job starvation? (Marco to follow-up with queueing team.)
- Should we expose a "cost-aware" preset that biases score towards cost, not latency? Product asked for this. (Priya + Sara to propose presets.)
- Worst-case path for KV cache coherence if we implement early-release (B) — risk needs kernel-level verification.
- Is 10% cost delta acceptable SLA for our enterprise customers? Finance/legal input required for downstream pricing notes.

Notes to self / lower-priority follow-ups:
- Add a tiny tracer tag to identify the batch flush boundary in logs for later analysis.
- Explore whether tokenizers' batching boundary (subtoken vs token) matter for short/long detection.
- Consider adding an offline ML-based length predictor as follow-up (after B prototype proves safe).

Reference snippets from discussion:
- Priya: "We can tune the timer aggressively for small routes - 4ms flush - and relax to 20ms for cost-focused routes. Having per-route default presets simplifies this for customers."
- Marco: "If we can make metrics cheap and presentable, product will opt more routes quickly; visibility matters more than perfect tuning."
- Chen: "Our canary rollback drills must include noisy neighbor scenarios. If we don't test that we'll get surprised in dedicated pools."

Decisions captured for RFC update:
- Update RFC-78 to reflect: (1) selected hybrid approach; (2) must-have metrics/alerts; (3) staged rollout plan; (4) parallel prototype for predictive early-release (B) tracked as tech-debt RFC.
- Owner for RFC update: Aisha (update by 2025-11-13).

Next meeting / checkpoints:
- Weekly sync (30m) on progress: Mondays 09:30 PST starting 2025-11-10. Focus: branch status, bench results, infra readiness.
- Canary kickoff: target 2025-11-30 (depends on Phase0/1 progress).

Attachments / artifacts produced during meeting:
- Inline simulator graphs (Ben) saved to benchboard link above.
- Initial scoring pseudocode (Ethan) in PR #1045.
- Draft console knobs mock (Sara) in product doc link.

If anything is wrong / you disagree with a decision, please reply on this doc or DM me in Slack (#eng-serving-runtime). Will update RFC once we have all action items closed.

-- Aisha
